lessons.title: Understanding Assumptions
lessons.concept: An assumption is something taken for granted or supposed to be true in a statement/argument, even if not explicitly stated. In statement-assumption questions, you must identify which assumption(s) are implicit and necessary for the statement to make sense.
lessons.formula: Test: If the assumption is false, does the statement lose its basis or purpose? If yes, it is implicit.
lessons.worked_example: Statement: 'Please switch off the lights when leaving the room.' Assumption: Lights consume electricity / keeping lights on unnecessarily is undesirable. This is implicit because the request is made to save power/avoid waste.
mistakes: Treating general knowledge as an assumption when it is not required by the statement
Choosing assumptions that are too extreme or far-fetched
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Implicit vs Explicit Ideas
lessons.concept: Explicit information is directly stated. Implicit assumptions are unstated but necessary. A valid assumption should be closely connected to the statement and not introduce new, unrelated ideas.
lessons.formula: Implicit assumption: necessary and unstated. Not implicit: explicitly stated, irrelevant, or merely possible but not required.
lessons.worked_example: Statement: 'Use this app to book tickets quickly.' Explicit: app can book tickets. Implicit: booking tickets quickly is desirable or possible through this app compared to alternatives.
mistakes: Marking restatements of the statement as assumptions
Assuming details that are possible but not necessary
Bringing outside opinions not supported by the statement
lessons.provenance: Authored original lesson; not scraped. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

lessons.title: Evaluating Multiple Assumptions
lessons.concept: Some questions provide two assumptions and ask whether I, II, both, or neither are implicit. Evaluate each assumption independently against the statement. An assumption can be valid even if the other is not.
lessons.formula: Check assumption I independently; check assumption II independently; then choose: only I, only II, both, either, or neither as per options.
lessons.worked_example: Statement: 'Students should practice mock tests to improve exam performance.' Assumption I: Practice can improve performance (implicit). Assumption II: Mock tests are the only way to improve performance (too strong, not implicit). So only I is implicit.
mistakes: Assuming both are implicit because one is clearly true
Accepting absolute words like 'only/always/never' without support
Failing to test each assumption separately

practice.question:

Assumption: Wearing a helmet can improve safety.
practice.explanation: The advice to wear a helmet is based on the implicit assumption that helmets provide protection/improve safety.

practice.question:
Statement: 'Candidates are advised to reach the exam center 30 minutes early.' Which assumption is implicit?
Assumption: Reaching early may help candidates complete pre-exam formalities on time.

options.C: Both statement and assumption are conclusions

practice.explanation: The advice implies that arriving early is beneficial, likely for formalities or avoiding delay, so this assumption is implicit.

practice.question:
Statement: 'Company X has launched a new training program for employees.'
Assumptions:
I. Training can help improve employee skills.
II. All employees lack skills.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
practice.explanation: Launching training implicitly assumes it can improve skills/performance (I). Saying all employees lack skills (II) is an extreme claim not implied.

Assumption: Reading instructions can help avoid mistakes during the test.
practice.explanation: The instruction to read carefully implies that doing so is useful and may help prevent errors or confusion.

practice.question: In statement-based reasoning, an assumption is:

options.A: A fact explicitly proved with data
options.B: Something implicitly taken for granted as true by the speaker
options.C: A conclusion the reader disagrees with
options.D: A statistical figure cited in the statement

practice.explanation: An assumption is an unstated premise the speaker relies on; it is not directly expressed but is necessary for the statement to hold.
practice.provenance: Authored for BountyCode as original practice/question item; not scraped from third-party sources. Requires independent verification before TRUSTED promotion.

practice.question: A common technique to test whether an assumption is necessary is to:

options.A: Negate it and see if the statement's conclusion still holds
options.B: Double the length of the statement

practice.explanation: The negation test: if denying the assumption weakens or destroys the conclusion, the assumption is necessary; if the conclusion survives, it is not necessary.

questions.question:

Assumption: Cycling can help reduce traffic congestion.
questions.explanation: The recommendation is meaningful only if cycling can contribute to reducing congestion; hence this assumption is implicit.

questions.question:
Statement: 'The school has introduced extra classes for students who need support in mathematics.'
Assumptions:
I. Some students may need additional support in mathematics.
II. Extra classes can help those students improve.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: Introducing extra classes for students who need support assumes both that such students exist (I) and that extra classes can help them (II).

questions.question:
Statement: 'Employees are encouraged to use public transport to reduce fuel expenses.'
Assumptions:
I. Using public transport may reduce fuel expenses.
II. Public transport is available to all employees at all times.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?
questions.explanation: The encouragement is based on possible reduction in fuel expenses (I). Claiming availability to all employees at all times (II) is too absolute and not implied.

questions.question: Statement: 'The company opened a new branch in the city.' Which of the following is a necessary assumption?

options.A: The branch will definitely be profitable
options.B: The company has the resources to run the new branch
options.C: Every customer will visit the branch daily
options.D: All employees prefer the new city

questions.explanation: Opening a branch presupposes resources (staff, funds, space) to run it. Profitability, daily visits, and employee preferences are not required for the action to be taken.

questions.question: Statement: 'The government should provide free laptops to students to improve education.' Which is a necessary assumption?

options.B: Students can use laptops meaningfully given basic supporting infrastructure
options.C: Every student already owns a smartphone

questions.explanation: The proposal assumes laptops will actually be usable to aid learning (electricity, connectivity, basic digital literacy). Guaranteed marks and existing devices are not assumed.

questions.question: Statement: 'Since the roads were flooded, the trains were cancelled.' Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the statement?

options.A: The flooding disrupted travel in the area
options.B: Trains run on the same roads as cars
options.C: Commuters were affected by the cancellation

questions.explanation: The statement assumes flood disrupted travel and affected commuters, but it does not assume trains run on roads (trains run on rails; that is false and not relied upon).
